description: Authoritative capability view of the suite: every action an agent may take, the credential that action requires, and every external service the automated pipeline may reach. data/ai-assets.json inventories the AI surfaces and docs/aims/third-party-register.md governs the vendor relationship (DPA, residency, data shared); THIS register governs what may be invoked, by whom, with which secret, and how it is revoked. The human view is docs/governance/tool-connector-register.md.
review_cadence: Quarterly with the AI asset register, and on any new action, credential, or egress host.

model_tool_calling.statement: No model call in this suite declares tools, tool_choice, or any function-calling parameter. Every model call is text-in / text-out: the model classifies, drafts, or advises, and deterministic code decides what happens next. There is therefore no path by which model output can invoke an action — the MCP-class risk of a model reaching a connector directly does not exist here, and re-opening it is a reviewable code change, not a configuration flip.
model_tool_calling.enforced_by: test/tool-register.test.mjs scans every model-API caller for tool-calling parameters and fails CI if one appears while this flag is false.

mcp_posture.statement: The suite exposes no Model Context Protocol server and ships no MCP client. Maintainers may reconcile the Asana workspace through MCP tooling in their own assistant (see docs/asana-integration-audit.md); that acts as the human, under the human's own Asana credential, and is reconciled by scripts/asana-reconcile.mjs like any other manual edit. No repository secret is ever handed to an MCP client.
mcp_posture.onboarding_rule: Adding an MCP server, a tool definition, or any new connector requires: a row in this register (action + credential + egress host + kill switch), a line in docs/aims/third-party-register.md if a new processor is involved, a DPIA delta if personal data crosses a new boundary, and MLRO approval recorded in the change. CI fails on an unregistered action or credential before the question of approval arises.

actions.purpose: Load the live customer base from the system of record.
Post the finished screening report. Carries no decision authority.
Grounded relevance/severity classification of a real headline. Dormant while LLM_TRIAGE=0.

Persist run state to the repository. Declared in the credential map but held by NO agent today — the map is deliberately wider than the allow-list so granting it is an explicit, reviewable edit rather than an omission.
Download designation lists. Public sources, no credential, no name sent.
Query public adverse-media and PEP sources. The subject name is the query; no customer record leaves the runner.
On-runner name matching against the downloaded lists.
Deterministic risk scoring and related-party detection.
Draft MLRO cases and STR content. PROPOSE only — the split from filing is the human-in-the-loop boundary.
Pre-publish integrity gate over the assembled report.

agents.name: PepAgent
agents.role: Detect PEP / RCA / SOE vs Wikidata

agents.name: DeliveryAgent
agents.role: Post the report to Asana (no decisions)

invariants: asana.write is held by DeliveryAgent alone — enforced at runtime by preflight_credentials() in agents.py, not only by this register.
state.commit is held by no agent; preflight_credentials() rejects it for anyone but DeliveryAgent should it ever be granted.
CaseAgent may propose but never file: no agent holds a filing action, because filing is an MLRO act.
The credential broker is the single authority that hands a secret to an agent, and only for an action that agent is authorized to take; every grant and denial is logged, the secret value never is.
An action outside an agent's allow-list is denied AND recorded — a denial is evidence, not a silent no-op.

connectors.purpose: Model inference for the three registered AI surfaces.
connectors.data_out: Advisor: officer question + optional pasted context. Triage: subject name + one public headline only. Reg-draft: public regulatory text. No customer record, ever.
kill_switches: LLM_TRIAGE=0 (triage stays dormant even with the key present)
REPORT_ALLOW_LLM=0 (no generative prose in filed reports)

connectors.purpose: Customer system of record (read) and report/case delivery (write).
connectors.credential_note: Two names by runtime, one workspace: the Python engine reads ASANA_TOKEN (screen.py requires it at import — the engine refuses to start rather than degrade silently), while the Node scripts and Netlify functions read ASANA_ACCESS_TOKEN. .github/workflows/netlify-deploy.yml bridges them (ASANA_TOKEN: secrets.ASANA_ACCESS_TOKEN || secrets.ASANA_TOKEN). Both are repository/site secrets; neither ever reaches the browser.
connectors.data_out: Customer records, UBOs, screening results — the system of record holds them by design.
kill_switches: unset the token (Python engine refuses to start; Node paths degrade loudly to a GitHub issue)

connectors.purpose: Run history, issue routing for degraded deliveries, state persistence.
connectors.data_out: Run metadata and alert text. No customer record is written to a public artefact.
kill_switches: workflow permissions are least-privilege per job; harden-runner egress allow-lists constrain every run

connectors.data_out: None — pull-only. No name is sent; matching happens on the runner.
kill_switches: core lists empty = DEGRADED fail-safe, never a silent clear

connectors.data_out: Subject name plus risk terms as a query string. No customer record.

connectors.purpose: PEP / RCA / SOE detection against Wikidata.
connectors.data_out: Individual name as a query. No customer record.

connectors.purpose: Change detection on public regulatory sources, with an Internet Archive fallback for hosts that block CI runners.
connectors.data_out: None — public pages are fetched by URL. The watched source list itself is governed in data/reg-sources.json, so adding a source is a reviewed data change.

connectors.purpose: Self-monitoring: currency, health and function probes against the firm's own published site.
connectors.data_out: None beyond the probe request itself; brain-soul.js uses the origin only for its CORS allow-list.
kill_switches: PRIMARY_ORIGIN / ALLOWED_ORIGINS bound which origins the functions answer

connectors.purpose: LEI entity reference data and INTERPOL notice checks.
connectors.data_out: Entity/individual name as a query. No customer record.
kill_switches: the checks are separate scripts/workflows and can be disabled independently

advisor_note: The MLRO Advisor is deliberately absent from the action table: it holds no action, no credential beyond the server-held model key, and no write path. It answers and stops. That is what makes it non-agentic in data/ai-assets.json, and any change to it belongs in this register first.
shadow_connector_note: No egress surface exists outside this register. test/tool-register.test.mjs cross-checks the action table and the agent roster against agents.py in both directions, verifies every declared credential is a real secret or environment variable, and fails CI if a model call ever declares tools while model_tool_calling.enabled is false.
